title: A tearful request for new bangles
odia:
ଆମ୍ବ ଗଛର ଶିଅ
ବୁଢା ଆଗେ ବୁଢୀ ସକେଇ କାନ୍ଦେ
ଖଡୁ ବଦଳେଇ ଦିଅ।
literal_meaning: The root of a mango tree; an old woman sobs before an old man: “Change my bangles for me.”
meaning_odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ଆଗରେ ବୁଢ଼ୀ ସକେଇ କାନ୍ଦି ଖଡ଼ୁ ବଦଳାଇ ଦେବାକୁ କହୁଛି। ବୟସ ବଢ଼ିଲେ ବି ଅଳଙ୍କାର ବଦଳାଇବାର ଇଚ୍ଛା ରହିବାକୁ ନେଇ ଏକ ଥଟ୍ଟାର ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଏହାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The main scene is a tearful request to exchange bangles. Calling both figures old brings age into the joke, while the request shows the woman’s continuing interest in an ornament. This is an editorial reading of the scene, not a judgment that such a wish is improper in later life.
usage_example: When discussing a comic verse about an older character asking for a new ornament, a reader might compare this scene and its exaggerated pleading. This is a newly composed reading example.
cultural_context: ଶିଅ is read as root, and ଖଡୁ as a bangle or bracelet. The mango-root opening rhymes with the closing ଦିଅ; no further symbolic connection is established here. The text does not specify the bangles’ material, a marriage rite, or why they need changing.
